market.headline: Stocks are up slightly before the open (SPY 760.48, QQQ 689.80), but QQQ is still below its 20- and 50-day averages. The day turns on the 08:30 PPI, after a hot inflation reading already has the Fed worried, and on Nvidia's leadership crisis four days before its earnings.
watch: 08:30 PPI: inflation is already running hot. Another hot number pushes the 10-year yield (4.98) higher and hits tech first. Trade the reaction after 10:00, not the headline.
QQQ 680.94 (200-day average): holding above it keeps the rebound alive. Below it, a retest of the November low at 647.05 is likely.
SPY 764.43 (50-day average): a close above it means the rebound has legs. Failing there keeps SPY stuck between 753.67 and 763.04.

stocks.headline: CEO Jensen Huang resigned over a scandal tied to an alleged Chinese spy. The stock hit 148.80 on 4.5 times normal volume, closed at 166.19 and trades 169.13 premarket.
stocks.why: The close near the day's high, far above the 148.80 low, shows big buyers stepped in on the panic. The business has not changed: sales are up 106% and speeding up, the operating margin is 65%, forecasts are up 24% in 90 days, and the stock costs only 10.5 times next year's profit. What the scandal can still damage is China sales, because Huang argued for keeping them open, the Commerce Secretary will testify to the Senate, and Chinese AI stocks are already falling on fears of tighter limits. It also leaves the CFO running the company as interim CEO into the Nov 17 report. Analysts cut targets hard (Melius to Hold at 185, Craig-Hallum Hold at 180), and the fallout spreads: money is moving into AMD and AVGO, SMCI fell 11.3%, and AI-financing names like CRWV and ORCL trade under a shadow.

long_term.reason: A leader with fast-rising sales and profits at its cheapest price in 5 years. The scandal hits sentiment and China risk, not today's demand.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A formal ban on China sales, or a CEO search still unsettled after the Nov 17 report, would move it to Wait. So would a break below 148.80.
stocks.action: Don't buy the open at 169.13. Buy a first small piece only if it holds 166.19 after the first hour, and keep the rest for after the Nov 17 report.

levels.means: Above = Thursday's panic low is holding. Below = the selling isn't done, so stop buying.
Above = buyers still control the day and a starter buy is fine. Below = wait for the report.
Above = the scandal is mostly priced in. Below = the stock is still in repair mode.

stocks.headline: Up 44.7% in 5 days and 5.9% Thursday to 585.30 as the main winner of Nvidia's turmoil. It trades 2.4% lower at 571.07 premarket.
stocks.why: Buyers are moving AI-chip money from Nvidia to the clear number two, and the business backs it. Sales are up 45% and speeding up, the operating margin doubled from 9% to 18%, AMD has beaten forecasts five quarters running, and forecasts are up 15% in 90 days. BofA raised its target to 700. But at 126 times last year's profit the price already assumes a lot, and today's premarket drop shows traders taking profits after the run. A clean Nvidia report on Nov 17 would pull part of this money back.

long_term.reason: Growth and margins are getting better every quarter, but after a 44.7% week the price is ahead of the business.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A strong, calm Nvidia report on Nov 17 would send money back to Nvidia and push AMD down toward its 20-day average.
stocks.action: Don't chase. Owners hold, and new buyers buy only if it pulls back to 554.90 and holds there.

levels.means: Above = breakout toward the 658.52 high and the 658.5 analyst target. Below = it keeps consolidating.
Above = the rotation into AMD is intact and this is the buy zone. Below = the trade is unwinding.
Above = the trend is healthy. Below = the whole Nvidia-scandal gain is gone.
